title: Integrated microwave-assisted acetic acid pretreatment and endoglucanase-xylanase hydrolysis for nanocrystalline cellulose preparation☆
author: Lim, Foo
materials: MW-assisted AA pretreatment was conducted in a 50 mL screw-sealed Teflon pressure reactor, and heated using a self-modified microwave oven [Model: Samsung ME711K, Inner dimensions: 36 cm (L) × 33 cm (W) × 24 cm (H)], operating at a power density of 1000 W and a frequency of 2.45 GHz. The microwave setup was upgraded with digital timer-temperature control system, and a high-temperature Type-K thermocouple to enable precise monitoring of irradiation time and temperature throughout the microwave heating. The pretreatment process was conducted by mixing swollen TP sample (1 g) with 50 % AA solution (solid-to-liquid ratio of 1: 20 g/mL). The process was irradiated at 100 °C for 10 min under microwave heating. After completion of the reaction, the reactor was cooled to room temperature within the microwave chamber, and the resulting pulp was filtered and washed repeatedly with deionized (DI) water until a neutral pH (6–7) was achieved. The delignified slurry (TP-CFs) was centrifuged at 6000 rpm for 15 min, and stored at 4 °C for the subsequent enzymatic hydrolysis.

The enzymatic hydrolysis of nanocrystalline cellulose was conducted in a 100 mL screw-capped Erlenmeyer flask containing 2 % (w/w, dry substrate basis) delignified TP-CFs, 50 mM citrate buffer (adjusted to pH 4.8, measured using a multi-channel benchtop pH meter, Accumet XL 600, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and 0.01 % (w/w) sodium azide to inhibit microbial growth and contamination, with a total reaction volume of 50 mL. The enzyme loadings were 25 U/g substrate (TP-CFs) for endoglucanase and 50 U/g substrate (TP-CFs) for xylanase, which were introduced into the reaction mixture. Prior to hydrolysis, the suspension was homogenized using an ultrasonic bath (FB15057 Fisherbrand® Ultrasonicator) at 25 °C for 30 min to enhance fiber dispersion and enzyme accessibility. The mixture was subsequently incubated in a shaker incubator (Model NB-205, N-biotek, Korea) at 150 rpm and 50 °C for 5 h to ensure uniform enzyme distribution and facilitate selective degradation of amorphous cellulose domains.

steps.title: Swell biomass and filter
steps.instruction: Swell 1 g raw TP biomass in 20 mL deionized water (solid‑to‑liquid ratio = 1:20 g/mL) at 300 rpm, 30 °C for 30 min; vacuum‑filter to remove excess water and collect the solid for pretreatment.

steps.title: Microwave acetic acid pretreatment
steps.instruction: Mix the swollen TP (1 g) with 50 % acetic acid solution at a solid‑to‑liquid ratio of 1:20 g/mL in a 50 mL screw‑sealed Teflon pressure reactor (≤60 % of reactor volume); irradiate at 100 °C for 10 min using a 1000 W microwave oven; cool the reactor in‑chamber to room temperature; filter the resulting pulp and wash repeatedly with deionized water until the wash reaches pH 6–7; centrifuge the washed pulp at 6000 rpm for 15 min; store the delignified slurry (TP‑CFs) at 4 °C for enzymatic hydrolysis.

steps.title: Prepare enzymatic hydrolysis mixture
steps.instruction: In a 100 mL screw‑capped Erlenmeyer flask add delignified TP‑CFs to obtain a 2 % w/w (dry substrate basis) loading, 50 mM citrate buffer adjusted to pH 4.8, and 0.01 % w/w sodium azide; bring the total volume to 50 mL; add endoglucanase at 25 U per g substrate and xylanase at 50 U per g substrate.

steps.title: Ultrasonicate suspension
steps.instruction: Place the flask in an ultrasonic bath set to 25 °C and sonicate for 30 min to enhance fiber dispersion and enzyme accessibility.

steps.title: Incubate enzymatic hydrolysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the sonicated mixture in a shaker incubator at 150 rpm, 50 °C for 5 h to allow selective degradation of amorphous cellulose domains.

steps.title: Quench hydrolysis by boiling
steps.instruction: At the end of the 5 h incubation, heat the reaction mixture to 100 °C and boil for 5 min to inactivate the enzymes.

steps.title: Separate solid and liquid
steps.instruction: Filter the boiled mixture and centrifuge the filtrate at 6000 rpm for 15 min; collect the solid precipitate (milky‑white) and the liquid hydrolysate separately.

steps.title: Analyze reducing sugars
steps.instruction: Withdraw an aliquot of the liquid fraction and determine total reducing sugar concentration using the 3,5‑dinitrosalicylic acid (DNS) colorimetric assay (absorbance at 540 nm) according to Miller’s method.

steps.title: Wash solid to neutral pH
steps.instruction: Resuspend the solid precipitate and repeatedly wash with deionized water, centrifuging each time at 6000 rpm for 15 min, until the wash water reaches pH 6–7.

steps.title: Final sonication and drying
steps.instruction: Sonicate the washed nanocellulose suspension for 10 min, then oven‑dry at 50 °C in an air‑circulation oven to constant weight before further characterization.
